title: Saving for a First Home Now Takes Twice as Long
summary:
Buying a first home has become much harder for many American families, a new report says.

The Center for Responsible Lending, a research nonprofit, studied how long it takes renters to save money for a down payment and closing costs. A down payment is the first chunk of money a buyer pays toward a house. Closing costs are fees paid when the home loan is finalized.

The center found that a renter household with a middle, or median, income would now need about 16 years to save enough for a starter home. That is twice as long as in 2019, the last time the center did this calculation. For middle-income households earning roughly $50,000 to $120,000 a year, the wait has doubled to 12 years. For workers such as teachers, nurses, firefighters and police officers, it now ranges from 10 to 13 years.

Why the big change? Since 2019, home prices have jumped, and everyday costs like food, gas and health care have risen. Rents have climbed too, while renters' incomes have not kept up. Mortgage rates are also above 7%.

The report says the wait is so long that young children could grow up and leave home before their family saves enough. The time also differs by city, from 11 years in Houston to 24 years in Los Angeles.

The center wants more help for first-time buyers and more small, cheaper homes, such as townhomes. Even so, a survey by the center found that young adults still hope to own homes as much as earlier generations did.
why_it_matters: Owning a home is one of the main ways families build security, so a longer wait affects where families live and whether children grow up in a home their family owns.

Closing costs are fees a buyer pays when a home loan is finalized.
The median is the middle value in a list of numbers arranged from smallest to largest.
Mortgage rates are the interest charged on loans people take out to buy homes.
A nonprofit is an organization that works for a cause instead of to make money for owners.

background_read: Most people who buy a home borrow much of the money through a loan called a mortgage, which they repay over many years.
Lenders usually require buyers to pay part of the price up front as a down payment, plus fees called closing costs.
When home prices, rents and everyday costs rise faster than people's pay, it becomes harder for renters to save that money.
A starter home is a smaller, less expensive home that people often buy as their first.
